title: onprem: airgap offline bundle - vendor rke2 + ubuntu updates + rollback tooling
author: Aisha Coleman
release_notes: Updated on-prem airgap offline bundle to include vendored RKE2 artifacts for Ubuntu 22.04 + rollback helper scripts and TUF metadata updates. No breaking changes to installer CLI. Recommended for customers using RKE2 on Ubuntu in air-gapped environments.
description:
Motivation: Several customers running Redwood Private on Ubuntu with RKE2 requested a vendorized offline bundle that includes Ubuntu 22.04-compatible RKE2 artifacts and a safe rollback path for operator-managed upgrades. This PR builds on previous vendoring work (rke2/flatcar) and adds Ubuntu packaging, updated TUF metadata, and a lightweight rollback helper to simplify emergency rollbacks in air-gapped clusters.

What this PR does: 1) Adds vendored RKE2 binaries and manifests for Ubuntu 22.04 (rke2-v1.24.9, rke2-v1.25.4 variants) into the offline bundle layout under vendor/rke2/ubuntu/; 2) Integrates APT mirror metadata and pre-seeded package indices to support offline apt installs used by the installer; 3) Updates TUF delegation and timestamp files to include the new artifact sets and refreshes signatures; 4) Adds a rollback helper script (bin/rollback-rke2.sh) that coordinates kubeadm-safe node drains, KV cache flush, and reverts control-plane image tags to the previous pinned bundle; 5) Adds unit tests for bundle validation and end-to-end smoke test config for the private-installer CI; 6) Expands the offline bundle build pipeline to produce a "rollback-manifest.json" artifact consumed by the installer at upgrade-time.

Checklist: - [x] Vendor RKE2 Ubuntu artifacts and manifests - [x] Add apt mirror indices and tarballs - [x] Update TUF metadata and re-sign root/delegations - [x] Implement rollback helper and docs - [x] Add bundle validation tests - [x] Run full offline-bundle CI and verify install/upgrade/rollback paths

Notes and caveats: - The vendored RKE2 builds are reproducible but large; we kept the bundle delta for Ubuntu under 1.2GB by pruning legacy debug artifacts. - Rollback helper requires operator privileges and assumes the cluster control plane was upgraded using the same bundle; it is intentionally conservative (refuses to rollback across major version gaps). - Customers using Flatcar or CoreOS-derived distros are unaffected by the Ubuntu artifacts but the TUF metadata covers multiple distro delegations.

Testing: Local bundle build + vm-based onboarding tests, CI offline-bundle pipeline (initial run failed due to a missing apt index file; fixed in commit 3), and a staged dry-run of the rollback helper against a non-production RKE2 cluster in our QA environment. CI shows full pass after the second pipeline run.

Related: builds on previous PRs that added RKE2 vendoring and flatcar updates (see pr-71234, pr-67123). References Linear tickets ENG-1423, ENG-1487 and support ticket SUP-983.
